title: Triangular coordinate change makes a formal series regular on an axis
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak m$ a maximal ideal of $A$, and $d\geq1$. Put $B=A[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For $f\in B$, write $\bar f\in(A/\mathfrak m)[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ for coefficientwise reduction. If $\bar f\ne0$, there are integers $e_i\geq2$ for $1\leq i<d$ such that the substitutions $X_i\mapsto X_i+X_d^{e_i}$ and $X_d\mapsto X_d$ define an $A$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $B$, with inverse given by $X_i\mapsto X_i-X_d^{e_i}$ and $X_d\mapsto X_d$, and $\overline{\sigma(f)}(0,\ldots,0,X_d)\ne0$. Substitution is interpreted by coefficientwise summation in the variable-adic topology. The case $d=1$ uses the identity automorphism. No infinitude or perfection assumption on $A/\mathfrak m$ is imposed.

proof.text: Write $\bar f=\sum_\beta c_\beta X^\beta$ and let $S=\{\beta\in\mathbf N^d:c_\beta\ne0\}$, which is nonempty. Choose $\alpha$ by successively minimizing the first coordinate in $S$, then the second among those with the chosen first coordinate, and so on. Every restricted set is nonempty; after $d$ choices $\alpha\in S$. Every $\beta\in S\setminus\{\alpha\}$ has a first differing coordinate $j$ with $\beta_j\ge\alpha_j+1$. Set $w_d=1$ and, backwards for $i<d$, set $w_i=2+\sum_{k>i}w_k\alpha_k$. For that first differing $j$, $$\sum_iw_i(\beta_i-\alpha_i)\ge w_j-\sum_{k>j}w_k\alpha_k>0.$$ For $j=d$ the right side is $1$; otherwise it is $2$. Thus $\alpha$ is the unique member of $S$ of minimal weight. Put $e_i=w_i\ge2$. This is successive minimization in $\mathbf N$ followed by the displayed integer inequality; it requires neither finiteness of $S$ nor any assumption on the coefficients.

proof.text: Put $J=(X_1,\ldots,X_d)\subset B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete], $B$ is $J$-adically complete. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] with $C=A$, $T=B$, the constant coefficient inclusion, and the tuples $b_i^+=X_i+X_d^{e_i}$, $b_i^-=X_i-X_d^{e_i}$ for $i<d$, and $b_d^+=b_d^-=X_d$. Every entry belongs to $J$. We obtain continuous ring maps $\sigma,\tau:B\to B$ fixing $A$, hence $A$-algebra maps, with the prescribed generator values. Their explicit truncation formulas are precisely coefficientwise substitution: modulo $J^N$ only input monomials of total degree less than $N$ contribute.

proof.text: Both composites $\sigma\tau$ and $\tau\sigma$ are continuous and fix constants. They fix $X_d$, and on $X_i$ for $i<d$ the two corrections cancel: $\sigma(X_i-X_d^{e_i})=X_i+X_d^{e_i}-X_d^{e_i}=X_i$, and $\tau(X_i+X_d^{e_i})=X_i-X_d^{e_i}+X_d^{e_i}=X_i$. The uniqueness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] for the tuple $(X_i)$ identifies both composites with the identity. Thus $\sigma$ is an automorphism with inverse $\tau$. For $d=1$ both tuples are $(X_1)$, so the same uniqueness gives the identity directly.

proof.text: Let $k=A/\mathfrak m$ and $T=k[[t]]$. It is $(t)$-adically complete by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-variables-complete]. Coefficientwise reduction and setting $X_1,\ldots,X_{d-1}$ to zero and $X_d=t$ are ring maps: coefficientwise this follows by distributing the finite convolution sums in [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $q:B\to T$ for their composite. It sends $J^N$ into $(t)^N$, so it is continuous. The composite $q\sigma$ agrees on $A$ and the variables with the evaluation map of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] for the tuple $(t^{w_1},\ldots,t^{w_d})$. By uniqueness the maps agree. Its truncation formula therefore gives, for each $N\ge0$, $$[t^N]q\sigma(f)=\sum_{\beta:\,\sum_iw_i\beta_i=N}c_\beta.$$ Indeed use truncation modulo $(t)^{N+1}$; weights are positive, so every exponent in this sum has $|\beta|\le N$, and the finite polynomial truncation suffices. A multiple of $t^{N+1}$ has no coefficient in degree $N$, directly from the convolution definition.

proof.text: Take $N=\sum_iw_i\alpha_i$. Step 1 shows that among the nonzero $c_\beta$ exactly $c_\alpha$ occurs in the sum of Step 4. Consequently $[t^N]q\sigma(f)=c_\alpha\ne0$. Since $q\sigma(f)$ is exactly $\overline{\sigma(f)}(0,\ldots,0,t)$, this proves the required nonvanishing. The argument uses only the nonempty support and finite sums, so works over finite or imperfect residue fields as well.

Step 1 takes the lexicographically least supported exponent alpha and sets w_d=1, w_i=2+sum_{k>i} w_k alpha_k; the weight gap is at least 1 or 2, so alpha is the unique weight minimiser and e_i>=2. Steps 2-3 apply lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation (C=A, T=B, I=J): the entries lie in J, B is J-complete by the variables-complete leaf, and the uniqueness clause gives the two-sided inverse. The composites are continuous because the forall-N-exists-M continuity condition composes. Step 4: q: B->k[[t]] is a ring map (on-axis convolution) with q(J^N) in (t)^N. By uniqueness q.sigma equals evaluation at t^{w_i}, and truncation modulo t^{N+1} gives coefficient sum_{w.beta=N} c_beta; since every w_i>=1, all such beta have |beta|<=N and are included. Step 5 leaves only c_alpha nonzero. Tested d=1, a nonzero constant, X_1-X_2^2 in characteristic 2 (image t^4-t^2) and X_1X_2. The parent's step 2 needs exactly sigma as an automorphism plus axis nonvanishing, which the item gives. Not duplicates: lem-per-weierstrass-henselian-cylinder does the same trick inline only under complete Noetherian local domain hypotheses, and lem-trf-formal-transverse-shift-calculus is characteristic 0 only. lean.statement: theorem exists_triangular_axis_coordinate_change {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (m : Ideal A) [m.IsMaximal] (n : ℕ) (f : MvPowerSeries (Fin (n + 1)) A) (hf : MvPowerSeries.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk m) f ≠ 0) : ∃ e : Fin n → ℕ, (∀ i : Fin n, 2 ≤ e i) ∧ ∃ σ : MvPowerSeries (Fin (n + 1)) A ≃ₐ[A] MvPowerSeries (Fin (n + 1)) A, (∀ g : MvPowerSeries (Fin (n + 1)) A, σ g = MvPowerSeries.subst (Fin.lastCases (MvPowerSeries.X (Fin.last n)) (fun i : Fin n => MvPowerSeries.X i.castSucc + MvPowerSeries.X (Fin.last n) ^ e i)) g) ∧ (∀ g : MvPowerSeries (Fin (n + 1)) A, σ.symm g = MvPowerSeries.subst (Fin.lastCases (MvPowerSeries.X (Fin.last n)) (fun i : Fin n => MvPowerSeries.X i.castSucc - MvPowerSeries.X (Fin.last n) ^ e i)) g) ∧ MvPowerSeries.subst (fun i : Fin (n + 1) => if i = Fin.last n then (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries (A ⧸ m)) else 0) (MvPowerSeries.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk m) (σ f)) ≠ 0 ∧ (n = 0 → σ = AlgEquiv.refl)
